findings.summary: The chapter's closing statement of spirit, and its account of why the volumes exist, were both removed.

evidence.baseline: This is the deepest reason these volumes exist. They are not a finished blueprint handed down to be implemented. They are an invitation to collective intelligence: a naming of the real problems, including the ones we do not yet know how to solve.
evidence.shipped: Open infrastructure is built through many contributions. The invitation should be specific: researchers can test claims, engineers can strengthen local processing.

findings.authorizedBy: Compression, and the volume card's Level 3 licence on pitch language.
findings.diagnosis: The shipped version issues a list of who may contribute what. The baseline says why the work is published at all: it is not a blueprint but an invitation, and it names the unsolved problems deliberately so others can solve them. That is the volume's account of its own genre, and it is the passage CTD-0045 would cite. The Level 3 licence targets pitch; this is not pitch, it is the statement of method.

findings.summary: The claim the section is titled for was deleted.

evidence.baseline: build it where the civilization's full intelligence can be brought to bear: one genius, one solved problem, one contributed line at a time.

findings.diagnosis: The heading diagnostic in its purest form: the section is named One Genius at a Time and the shipped text contains neither the phrase nor the idea. What survives, the construction remains work for many hands, is the same thought with the image removed, and the image is what makes the claim about distributed genius rather than about labour supply.

findings.summary: The handoff to Volume IV lost its specificity.

evidence.baseline: the specific technical architecture of the identity layer, the trust layer, and the on-device system; the precise standards and protocols; the engineering decisions that turn these principles into a working instrument.
evidence.shipped: The construction remains work for many hands, under standards that let every hand be questioned.

findings.diagnosis: The baseline names three specific deliverables it expects the next volume to supply. That is a checkable promise, and CTD-0047 exists because it may not have been kept. Removing the list removes the ability to check.

evidence.baseline: the right principles fenced around a four-item list, an invitation to collective intelligence, brought to bear, and The construction of that openness fenced around a three-part list.

findings.diagnosis: One fenced a four-item list mid-sentence and was rebuilt by splitting the sentence so the principles land after a colon. Two introduced specifications and became colons. One fenced a three-part semicolon list between a subject and its verb and was rebuilt so the claim completes and the list follows after a colon, with the internal semicolons intact.

debtImpact.note: The promise that the next volume specifies, at the level a builder could act on, how the instrument is constructed, returns with its three named deliverables. The item exists because Volume IV defers part of this. The promise is now checkable again.
The restored handoff states what Volume III expects Volume IV to contain, which is the inventory the item asks for.

The restored close is an invitation to everyone with the genius and the care to help. It is the volume's warmest recruitment passage outside the failure chapter, and the balance the item records as an author decision is live here.
The history of every great open project is the history of many hands is an unbounded historical claim.
